- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment — adjust downward bias by +0.5–1.0% relative to recent mean.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Lagged mean reversion: if sentiment shows reversal after 3–5 days of strong bullishness, reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment volatility — smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 sentiment-adjusted values.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- Forecast should not exceed 2 standard deviations above recent 10-day mean unless sentiment is strongly bullish and confirmed.
